Draft 1: Windsor, a project story (10 photos, in order)

A+

Out with the old block edging. In with one continuous curb. This Windsor yard had old concrete block edging along the beds. On day one, our crew pulled the blocks out and hand-carved more than 250 feet of Natural Stone curb, then dug a path through the garden arch, laid fabric and river rock, and set flagstone steppers on top. One week later we came back to seal the curb. Compare photo 3 on day one with photo 5, the same bed sealed: darker, with a glossy finish. Swipe through to see it go from day one to done 👉 Thinking about your beds for next season? Send us a message or call 608-220-2224. #WindsorWI #CurbEdging #Landscaping #Hardscape

Draft 2: Same curb, one week apart (2 photos)

A+
A+ Lawn Care LLC
Draft · Public
Same curb, one week apart. Can you spot the difference? Left: day one, right after our crew hand-carved this Natural Stone curb in Windsor. Right: seven days later, after we came back and sealed it. The seal darkens the colors and gives the curb its glossy finish. Every A+ curb gets one application of sealant about a week after it's installed, and that visit is included. What's inside matters too: fiber mesh and a hardener in the concrete mix, plus galvanized steel cable the entire length of the curb. Questions about curb edging? Ask us in the comments or call 608-220-2224. #CurbEdging #ConcreteCurbing #WindsorWI

455 feet of curb in one DeForest yard 🌿 This yard had vegetable gardens, raised planters and a stone-wall garden, with no edge between the lawn and the beds. Our crew took out sod, dug in 10 feet of drain tile out front, and poured 455 feet of Natural Stone curb around the house and the garden beds, in earth tones with charcoal. Two weeks later we came back and sealed it. Swipe from before to after 👉 Want a clean edge around your beds next season?
